facts.program: Efficiency Vermont heat pump rebates
facts.claim: Ductless heat pump: $375 off up to 2 tons, $475 off over 2 tons (instant discount, effective Jan 1, 2026), plus up to $600 for integrated controls. Ducted heat pump: $1,200 off up to 2 tons, $1,700 over 2 and under 4 tons, $2,200 at 4 tons or more (effective April 1, 2025).
facts.eligibility: Vermont electric customers; qualifying cold-climate equipment
facts.notes: Read on efficiencyvermont.com ductless, ducted and integrated-controls pages 2026-10-03.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont income bonus (heat pumps)
facts.claim: Income bonus on heat pumps, $200 to $2,200 depending on utility and income level: Green Mountain Power low-income $2,200; VPPSA municipal utilities moderate or low income $1,000; all other utilities $200. Rental property owners and Burlington Electric customers are not eligible for this bonus. 2026 income limits effective July 1, 2026.
facts.eligibility: Low/moderate income per Efficiency Vermont guidelines
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-03. The '$7,950' figure once shown on GMP-territory city pages came from Burlington Electric content; no source supports it for Green Mountain Power customers.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power income-eligible heat pump rebate
facts.claim: GMP pays an income-eligible heat pump rebate of $2,000 per condenser to customers at or below 80% of area median income, combined with the Efficiency Vermont rebate in one application made through Efficiency Vermont's site. 2026 80% AMI limits for a household of four: $92,150 Addison County, $99,750 Chittenden, Franklin and Grand Isle, $91,200 Washington, $89,200 other counties.
facts.eligibility: GMP customers at or below 80% AMI
facts.notes: Old URL greenmountainpower.com/heat-pump-rebate/ is gone (404); current page read 2026-10-03.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont heat pump water heater
facts.claim: Heat pump water heater: $600 discount or rebate, plus $400 more for income-eligible households, up to $1,000 (effective Aug 16, 2025). GMP's own page points to Efficiency Vermont for up to $600.
facts.eligibility: Vermont homeowners

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont Home Performance with ENERGY STAR (weatherization)
facts.claim: 75% of qualifying insulation and air-sealing project cost, up to $3,000; up to $7,000 for low and moderate income households whose property is their primary residence (effective July 1, 2026, while funding lasts). Needs an Efficiency Excellence Network contractor and at least a 10% blower-door air leakage reduction. Burlington Electric and Vermont Gas customers are paid by their own utility, up to $9,500 for a single-family home.
facts.eligibility: Existing 1 to 4 unit Vermont homes; Efficiency Excellence Network contractor
facts.notes: Replaces the earlier $4,000/$9,500 figure, which came from the January 2026 announcement and is out of date. The $9,500 figure now applies to Burlington Electric and Vermont Gas customers.

facts.program: Electric utility by city
facts.claim: Barre, Montpelier, Rutland and South Burlington are Green Mountain Power territory; Burlington is Burlington Electric Department.
facts.notes: Per the pre-clobber hub pages and city-rebate-lookup.json.

facts.program: Burlington Electric Department heat pump offers
facts.claim: Burlington Electric customers: up to $2,900 on a ductless heat pump and up to $8,750 on a ducted system as a post-purchase rebate, plus discounts of $350 to $450 (ductless) and $1,000 to $2,000 (ducted) and up to $1,200 on a heat pump water heater, listed as partner offers on the Efficiency Vermont pages.
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric Department customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-03 under Partner Offers on the ductless and ducted pages.

facts.program: Other Vermont utility partner offers
facts.claim: Stowe Electric $250 and Vermont Electric Co-op $150 thermal bonus on ductless heat pumps; VPPSA municipal utilities $200 weatherization rebate and $200 on heat pump water heaters.
facts.eligibility: Customers of those utilities
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-03 on the Efficiency Vermont ductless and water heater pages.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont ground source heat pumps
facts.claim: Up to $2,100 per ton cash back on qualifying ground source heat pumps, plus a $500 bonus for income-eligible Vermonters. New systems up to 10 tons; wood-heating customers not eligible; Efficiency Excellence Network contractor.
facts.eligibility: Vermont electric customers; Hyde Park Electric customers may not get the full amount

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont smart thermostat and appliance rebates
facts.claim: Smart thermostat up to $100; clothes dryer up to $400 (washer-dryer combination $400); window air conditioner $150; wood or pellet stove $400 at purchase; dehumidifier from $25; Home Energy Loan from 0% interest; free products for income-qualified Vermonters.
facts.eligibility: Vermont residents
facts.notes: Residential list read 2026-10-03.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power Bring Your Own Device (home battery)
facts.claim: GMP pays $850 per kW of storage enrolled for a three-hour battery discharge or $950 per kW for four hours, set by how much stored energy you agree to share during peaks (a few times a month). Retrofitting an existing solar system in an area where storage helps most earns an extra $100 per kW. Listed batteries: Duracell, Eguana, Emporia, Enphase IQ, Fortress, FranklinWH, NeoVolta, Savant 20 and 50, SolarEdge StorEdge compatible systems, Tesla Powerwall 2 and 3. GMP also lists a Lease Energy Storage option whose terms were not read.
facts.eligibility: Green Mountain Power customers with a listed battery
facts.notes: Read in browser pane 2026-10-05. Enrollment caps and end date not stated on the page text read ("See All Details & Requirements" not opened). Lease program page could not be read, so no lease terms are used.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power electric vehicle rebates
facts.claim: All-electric vehicle: new purchase $1,500, new lease $1,000, used purchase or lease $1,000. Plug-in hybrid: new purchase $1,000, new lease $750, used $750. Income-eligible customers (80% of Vermont statewide median income; $94,672 for four people) get an extra $1,000 on an all-electric vehicle, up to $2,500 total. Valid for qualifying vehicles purchased or leased through December 31, 2026. Some dealers apply it as a discount; rebates may be taxable income.
facts.eligibility: Green Mountain Power customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. 80% SMI limits 1 person $66,255 through 8 people $124,970.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power home Level 2 charger program
facts.claim: Buy or lease an EV in 2026 and get a check up to $500 toward charger installation once the GMP charger is connected and enrolled in a discount charging rate (cannot exceed the installation receipt), plus $150 off the install through Treehouse. GMP page headline: installation incentives up to $650. Needs an EV registered at the GMP account address, a smart meter, reliable wifi, and home ownership or landlord approval.
facts.eligibility: Green Mountain Power customers with an EV
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. The electric-vehicles landing page says the charger itself is free while in the Home Charging program; the charger page does not state that, so we do not repeat it.

facts.program: Burlington Electric Department electric vehicle rebates
facts.claim: New or leased electric vehicle $5,000; new plug-in hybrid $2,000; used or pre-owned EV or plug-in hybrid $1,300; income-qualified customers get an additional amount (gross income limit $99,750 for a household of four; $69,850 for one). Separate programs exist for high-mileage drivers (17,600 miles a year or more).
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. Extra income-qualified amount is on BED rebate form, not read.

facts.program: Burlington Electric home EV charger rebate and EV rate
facts.claim: Rebate of up to $900 for a home charger, set by the EV purchased; currently only the ChargePoint Home Flex charger qualifies. EV Rate credit of 8.7894 cents per kWh lowers charging to 9.95 cents per kWh (about 75 cents a gallon by BED math, 45% savings); charging only between 10 pm and noon on the Fixed Schedule option or in hours BED announces on the Flexible Load option, or the month credit is lost. Multi-family properties get $1,000 per qualifying charger setup; workplaces $2,500 per port up to 75% of cost.
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric Residential Service customers with wifi and a qualifying charger
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05, with the EV rate page https://www.burlingtonelectric.com/evrate. The rate page also mentions a refund of up to $1,000 on charger and installation; the charger page says $900, so we use $900.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power appliance and yard rebates
facts.claim: Induction cooktop or range $200 (installed, not portable; purchases through December 31, 2026; one per account); electric lawn tractor $100, push mower $50, electric trimmers, leaf blowers and chainsaws $25; heat pump water heater up to $600 through Efficiency Vermont.
facts.eligibility: Green Mountain Power customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05 on the landing page and the induction cooktop and heat pump water heater pages. Lawn and yard amounts from the landing page text.

facts.program: Green Mountain Power net metering
facts.claim: Net metering lets Vermonters send unused solar power to the grid and pay only for the difference; surplus in a month becomes a credit toward the next bill; credits more than one year old expire; net metering is meant to cover a customer's own use, not exceed it.
facts.eligibility: GMP customers with a grid-tied system
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. A web-search summary of GMP tariffs quoted per-kWh solar credit rates, but we did not read the tariff itself, so no rate is used.

facts.program: Burlington Electric solar and net metering rules
facts.claim: BED says solar systems run $3 to $7 per watt and an average BED residential customer's system makes 35% to 50% of annual use; net metering needs a grid connection and a separate generation meter (about $150 residential) installed by BED; systems over 15 kW need BED interconnection approval before the state Certificate of Public Good registration; city permits and a Department of Public Works electrical inspection are required before BED energizes it.
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. No BED solar rebate is listed on this page or the rebates page.

facts.program: Vermont Gas weatherization rebates
facts.claim: Single-family homes: market-rate households 50% of project up to $4,000; moderate income 75% up to $7,000; low income 90% up to $9,500. Townhouse and condo 75% up to $1,000 per unit; multi-family 50% up to $10,000 (75% when tenants pay the gas bill); manufactured homes 75% up to $4,875 or $2,850 depending on scope. Needs a BPI-certified contractor and at least a 10% air leakage reduction; projects complete by December 31, 2026.
facts.eligibility: Vermont Gas customers (Burlington and South Burlington gas heat)
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. Vermont Gas, not Efficiency Vermont, pays for gas-heated homes. BED says gas customers should call VGS.

facts.program: Vermont Gas weatherization financing and WRAP
facts.claim: Green Mountain Credit Union loans up to $20,000 over 5 years: 0% APR on weatherization projects; 5.99% APR when the project includes heat pumps. The Weatherization Repayment Assistance Program (WRAP) lets eligible customers repay through the VGS bill, and repayment stays with the gas meter if the home is sold.
facts.eligibility: Vermont Gas customers; subject to credit union approval
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. BED also lists WRAP for homeowners and renters on its weatherization page.

facts.program: Burlington Electric heat pump rebate tables
facts.claim: BED says its rebates cover up to 75% of installed cost. Centrally ducted standard systems: contractor point-of-sale discount $1,000 (up to 2 tons), $1,500 (over 2 to 4 tons), $2,000 (over 4 tons), plus a $500 BED bonus per condenser for qualifying customers. High performance ducted systems on the NEEP cold-climate list add a BED online rebate of $1,350, $3,950 or $5,450 by size. Air-to-water heat pump incentives total up to $12,400. BED warns that homes heated with natural gas might not save money with an air-source heat pump.
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. Efficiency Vermont lists the ductless offers (vt-6). Figures are BED's own; the $12,400 air-to-water figure is a total BED states without a table.

facts.program: Burlington Electric water heater offers
facts.claim: BED gives free tank wraps and low-flow showerheads to electric resistance water heater owners (saves up to $75 a year by BED), and tells heat pump water heater buyers to ask contractors about the $600 statewide discount. BED's rebate page lists contractor midstream heat pump water heater cash back up to $800 at HVAC distributors.
facts.eligibility: Burlington Electric customers
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05 with https://www.burlingtonelectric.com/rebates. Efficiency Vermont lists up to $1,200 for BED customers under partner offers (vt-6); BED's own pages do not state $1,200, so check with BED.

facts.program: Windows and doors in Vermont programs
facts.claim: Efficiency Vermont's residential rebate list read on 2026-10-05 has no window or door replacement rebate. Vermont Gas weatherization rebates have an FAQ about windows and doors that was not opened. BED advises talking to Energy Services before large window replacement and suggests storm windows, shrink kits and cellular shades first.
facts.notes: Absence checked against the full residential list; the Vermont Gas FAQ answer was not read, so we do not say Vermont Gas pays for windows or not.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont free and low-cost income-qualified offers
facts.claim: The residential list shows free appliances, products and services for income-qualified Vermonters, the free Income Qualified Weatherization Assistance Program (through a partner), a free Virtual Home Energy Visit, and $100 cash back for DIY weatherization (BED: three DIY projects).
facts.eligibility: Income-qualified Vermonters; DIY for residents
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. Detail tabs not opened; income limits not stated here.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont EV incentive listing
facts.claim: Efficiency Vermont lists electric vehicle incentives of up to $5,700 and EV charging offers, both delivered through partner utilities; requirements differ by program and utility, and many dealers pass the incentive through at purchase.
facts.eligibility: Varies by utility
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. The $5,700 is the listing headline for the largest utility offer, not a statewide amount; read each utility page for its own figures.

facts.program: Vermont Gas Clover Energy heat pump offers
facts.claim: Clover Energy by VGS offers heat pump lease and purchase, a Green Mountain Credit Union heat pump loan application, service plans and a coverage-area map. It installs ductless mini-splits, heat pump water heaters, and centrally ducted systems only for customers with a natural gas furnace (hybrid systems with a backup heat source).
facts.eligibility: Vermont Gas customers inside the Clover coverage area
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. No prices were on the page; the pricing sheet was not opened.

facts.program: Efficiency Vermont solar PV listing
facts.claim: Efficiency Vermont lists Solar Photovoltaic (PV) among its residential rebates pages but gives no dollar amount: the page has a Contact Us button and related articles on renewable energy, smart homes and net zero homes.
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. The Eligibility tab content did not load in the text view, so a dollar amount hidden there cannot be ruled out; call Efficiency Vermont to confirm.
